extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, IP managers, in-house counsel, patent attorneys, startups and companies seeking infringement analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on creating and using patent claim charts to evaluate infringement, map evidence to claim elements, and support litigation or IP strategy. Focuses on the components of a claim chart report and how it helps assess infringement, validity, and strategic options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim chart structure (split claims into elements in tabular form)
rubrics_metrics.description: A target patent claim is split into individual claim elements and represented in a tabular form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each claim element should be interpreted and evidence of use or prior art mapped correspondingly; evidences can include a patent, a product, or any published information. Claim charts are alternatively termed claims tables, infringement contentions (ICs), invalidity contentions, preliminary infringement contentions (PICs) depending on requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of claim elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the claim elements are interpreted individually to understand scope and limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable claim construction principles should be applied when interpreting elements so that mapping to accused product features is meaningful and defensible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence mapping to claim elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Map evidences of use or prior art directly to the corresponding claim elements in the chart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete sources (e.g., patents, products, published information) and cite technical resources to support each mapped element; ensure traceability from claim language to factual evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustive product search to identify potential infringers
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct an exhaustive product search to narrow down a list of potentially infringing products/services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search broadly across markets and suppliers to capture all candidate accused products before detailed mapping; this is a front-end step of the claim chart report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensive technical research for evidence gathering
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform extensive research to garner evidence from varied technical resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult data sheets, product manuals, technical articles, and other technical documentation to collect support for mapping claim elements to accused products/features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wide analysis of claim elements and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze each patent claim element and its limitations comprehensively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider not only literal elements but also dependent claims and limitations; identify ambiguities and potential constructions that affect scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed mapping onto accused product features using reasonable claim construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Map the patent claims onto the features of the accused product on the basis of reasonable claim construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the mapping shows how each claim limitation is present (or absent) in the accused product, using a defensible construction standard to support infringement or non-infringement positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a factual opinion on infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver an opinion on infringement supported by facts and findings from the comparison chart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The opinion should be grounded in the mapped evidence and explain how the evidence supports (or does not support) each claim element being met by the accused product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest workarounds and IP strategy based on chart outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer suggestions and workarounds for development of an IP strategy based on the results of the comparison chart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations may include design-around options, licensing opportunities, enforcement steps, or further prosecution/defensive measures informed by the strength of the mapped evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use claim charts to scrutinize claim scope to identify covered products/services
rubrics_metrics.description: Scrutinize the claims of a patent to identify the products and services covered by them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically compare claim language to market offerings to determine the universe of potentially covered products and services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use claim charts to evaluate patent validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine the claim elements of a patent to assess the validity of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mapping can reveal prior art or inconsistencies relevant to invalidity contentions; claim charts may be used as invalidity contentions when supporting challenges to validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support litigation tasks: narrow issues and advance discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Assist the court or parties' infringement contentions involved in litigation to narrow down the case so they can focus and advance discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-prepared claim charts help identify the precise disputed elements and factual questions, enabling targeted discovery and more efficient case management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gather facts to support or rebut Doctrine of Equivalence (DOE) arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Help the parties in finding the facts to support the argument against (or for) the Doctrine of Equivalence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mapping and technical evidence to show whether an accused product that does not literally meet a claim element nevertheless performs substantially the same function in substantially the same way to yield substantially the same result, or to refute such a claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess overall strength or weakness of a party's position
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the claim chart to evaluate the strength or weakness of a party's infringement or defense position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize vulnerabilities and strengths revealed by the mapping, evidence quality, and claim constructions to inform settlement, litigation, or licensing decisions.
